subject: Information Theory
title: The Double Helix as Backup
description: One-minute skill: The Double Helix as Backup.

hook.text: DNA is double-stranded. If one strand is damaged, the other serves as a template for repair. It's a built-in backup.

buildup.text: A pairs with T, C pairs with G. Each strand contains the complete information to reconstruct the other.

discovery.text: This is parity: each base's complement is determined, so one strand is a redundant copy. Total redundancy factor: 2.

twist.text: When both strands break at the same spot—a double-strand break—the backup fails. This is the most dangerous DNA damage.

climax.text: Homologous recombination can fix even double-strand breaks by using the sister chromosome as a template.

punchline.text: Two strands, one message. Redundancy is life's error correction.

quiz.question: Why is DNA double-stranded?
options: Each strand serves as a backup template for repairing the other
